title.narrative: Malawi Emergency Project to Protect Essential Health Services

description.narrative: The development objective of the Emergency Project to Protect Essential Health Services (EHS) Project for Malawi is to provide emergency support and enable the continued delivery of essential health services in Malawi. The project comprises of five components. The first component, protecting provision of frontline health service delivery will support the government to protect and sustain delivery of EHS. It consists of following sub-components: (i) support to frontline health workers; and (ii) support to frontline health facilities. The second component, provision of essential medicines will support the Ministry of Health (MoH) to address the issue of severe drug and medical supply shortage that Malawi is experiencing. The third component, enhancing the efficiency and accountability of public spending in the health sector will strengthen core institutional systems that relate to efficient service delivery and accountability in the health sector. The fourth component, project management will finance the operational costs of project implementation which will be prioritized around the emergency nature of the response. The fifth component, contingent emergency response component will allow for rapid reallocation of uncommitted funds in the event of an eligible emergency as defined in OP 8.00.
To provide emergency support and enable the continued delivery of essential health services in Malawi.

condition.narrative: Section 1.A.4.a of Schedule 2 to the FA: The Recipient shall not later than thirty (30) days from the Effectiveness Date establishand thereafter maintain throughout implementation of the Project, a Project Implementation Committee chaired by Chief of HealthServices of MoH and comprising: (i) Project Coordinator; (ii) Directors of relevant select departments and units of MoH ; (iii)Accountant General; (iv) Budget Director; (v) Director of Department of Human Resource Management; (vi) Director from Ministry ofLocal Government; (vii) Director from the National Local Government Finance Committee; (viii) Controller of Internal Audit Unit;(ix) Director from Central Medical Store Trust (CMST); and (x) Director from Christian Health Association of Malawi and allresponsible for ensuring the Project is implemented in accordance with agreed technical quality and teams comply with agreed policyguidelines.

Section 1.C.1 of Schedule 2 to the FA: The Recipient shall recruit, not later than sixty (60) days after the Effective Date, andthereafter maintain throughout Project implementation, an independent verification agent (“Verification Agent”) with qualification,experience and under terms of reference satisfactory to the Association to undertake the verification of compliance with the PBCsin accordance with the Verification Protocol.

Section 1.C.2 of Schedule 2 to the FA: The Recipient shall ensure that the Verification Agent, not later than thirty (30) daysafter the verification of compliance with or achievement of the PBCs for the pertinent calendar year has been completed, preparesand furnishes to the Recipient, who shall in turn furnish to the Association, a report on the results of said verification processof such scope and in such detail as the Association shall reasonably request.

Section 4.A of Schedule 2 to the FA: The Recipient shall on a quarterly basis prepare and submit satisfactory reports to theAssociation on the implementation of the MoH-DHRMD Payroll Controls Review and Action Plan.

Section 4.B of Schedule 2 to the FA: B. The Recipient shall no later than 30 days after the Effectiveness Date prepare and submitto the Association satisfactory Terms of Reference for a due diligence review of the Environmental and Social Quality ManagementSystem.

Section I.A.3.a and b of Schedule 2 to the FA: The Recipient shall no later than thirty (30) days from the Effectiveness Date,establish and thereafter maintain throughout the implementation of the Project, a Project Steering Committee comprising (i) thePrincipal Secretary of Administration at the MoH; and (ii) the Secretary for Human Resource Management and Development in DHRMDresponsible for providing strategic oversight and promote coordination and planning between the entities in the implementation andmonitoring of the Project activities. The PSC shall be chaired jointly by Secretary of Treasury and Secretary for Health andinitially meet every month for the next three months after the Effectiveness Date, and thereafter on a quarterly basis.
